questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

One should wear a mask while going out.

options.text: While going out a, mask will be worn.
While going out, a mask can be worn.
While going out, a mask should be worn.
While going out, a mask would be worn.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **While going out, a mask should be worn. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and we need to change it to the passive form.
 
• The active voice has the following form: **Subject + modal + verb 1 + object__**
 
• The passive voice has the following form: __Object + modal + be + verb 3 + by + Subject__
 __
 
• Active: *One should keep one's promises.*
 
• Passive: *Promises should be kept.*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the Subject into the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Passive Voice:__* **While going out, a mask should be worn. *

Rahul said, “I will start going to office from tomorrow.”

options.text: Rahul said that he would start going to office from the next day.

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech and we need to convert it into an indirect speech.
 
• We follow these rules in Direct-Indirect speech:
 
 
• The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' in the indirect speech.
 
• If the direct speech is written in the future continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)__ tense, then we have to change it into a conditional continuous tense __(Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)__ in the indirect speech. therefore:
 
 
• The modal verb 'will' in direct speech changes to 'would' in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the preposition 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is omitted to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech is in capital letters.
 
• **'Tomorrow'** becomes **'the next day'** in the indirect speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

The indirect sentence is: *Rahul said that he would start going to office from the next day. *

• When using **many**, the noun will always be **plural**.
 
• You can use **many **with a noncount noun only if you are talking about different types, kinds, or measured quantities of something.
 
 
• **Example -** *There are so **many **things to do I don’t know if we will get them all done.*
 
 
 
• *​*In the given sentence, "**advantages**" is mentioned so, '**many**' should be used as it refers to a plural noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which contains an error.

**Corrected sentence:** *There are **many **__advantages of working together in a group.*

• The "full stop" in the indirect speech changes to Exclamation Point ( ! ) in the direct speech.

Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

Hence, direct speech is - *Nidhi exclaimed in disappointment that she had missed the deadline for sending her application again.*
